answer: An agent economy can bind each identity to a scarce, nontransferable stake that is slashed when its signed actions violate a challengeable rule, such as submitting duplicate claims. Reputation and access grow only through verified work over time, so creating a hundred fresh agents does not create a hundred trusted voices. A sybil attacker must lock capital in every identity and risk losing it, while also paying the labor and delay needed to build history. A yarrow-market trial at the summit terrace could expose clones cheaply; the attacker still bears those stake and time costs.
